```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# NCAA OPPONENT ADVANCE REPORT
# ONE-FILE R MARKDOWN BUILD  ·  v2
# ============================================================
#
# WEEK-TO-WEEK WORKFLOW
# 1. Change TEAM_QUERY and SEASON below.
# 2. Leave REFRESH_DATA = FALSE for cached/repeat renders.
# 3. Set REFRESH_DATA = TRUE once when you want fresh data.
# 4. Click Knit.  Output is a single self-contained .html file
#    that can be emailed or posted as-is.
#
# WHAT CHANGED IN v2 (see the Data Quality tab in the report)
# - Season rate stats now come from the official NCAA source.
#   ESPN box scores are used only for the recent-game window.
#   The two are reconciled and disagreements are reported.
# - Every table states its source and its sample window.
# - Games that failed to download are counted and disclosed
#   instead of silently shrinking the sample.
# - Play-by-play events are attributed to the player who did
#   them, not to every name that appears in the sentence.
# ============================================================


# ============================================================
# 1. SETTINGS - THIS IS THE MAIN SECTION YOU CHANGE
# ============================================================

TEAM_QUERY <- "UCLA"
SEASON     <- 2026

# Most recent completed games used for the detailed
# player / lineup / pitching / bullpen / tendency analysis.
DETAIL_GAMES <- 20

# Recent-form comparison window.
RECENT_GAMES <- 10

# FALSE = use files already stored in cache/
# TRUE  = force the report to refresh its source data.
REFRESH_DATA <- FALSE

# Pull official NCAA season stats as a second source and
# reconcile them against ESPN.
#
# stats.ncaa.org is slow and throttles aggressively. This layer
# is time-boxed so it can never stall a knit: if it does not
# finish inside the budget below the report renders anyway and
# says so on the Data Quality tab. Once it succeeds it is cached
# and later knits are instant.
#
# Set USE_NCAA <- FALSE to skip it entirely.
USE_NCAA            <- TRUE
NCAA_DIVISION       <- 1
# Optional: paste a stats.ncaa.org team id here to skip lookup
# entirely. Find it in the URL of the team's stats page. Leave NA
# to let the report resolve it.
NCAA_TEAM_ID <- NA_character_

NCAA_TIMEOUT_SECONDS <- 60   # cap on any single NCAA request
NCAA_BUDGET_SECONDS  <- 180  # cap on the whole NCAA section

# Scraping the full Division I index off stats.ncaa.org takes
# minutes and is the only step here that can hang. It is OFF by
# default: the report resolves the team from tables bundled with
# baseballr instead, and if those miss it tells you to paste an id
# rather than spending three minutes discovering it cannot.
NCAA_ALLOW_INDEX_SCRAPE <- FALSE

# Network timeout for ESPN requests.
NET_TIMEOUT_SECONDS <- 120

# Minimum sample before a player appears in a ranked table.
# Anyone under the line still shows, in a separate
# "limited sample" table, so nobody silently disappears.
MIN_AB_WINDOW  <- 10   # hitters, at-bats in the window
MIN_OUT_WINDOW <- 9    # pitchers, outs recorded (9 outs = 3.0 IP)
MIN_PA_SEASON  <- 40   # hitters, season plate appearances

# ---- Top-three lists on the Game Plan tab -------------------
# Two separate lists, not one blended one. The season list answers
# "who are their best players"; the recent list answers "who is
# swinging it right now". Mixing those into a single ranking hides
# both answers.
RECENT_PERF_GAMES <- 5    # window for the recent-performers section
MIN_AB_RECENT     <- 6    # hitters, at-bats over that window
MIN_OUT_RECENT    <- 6    # pitchers, outs recorded (6 outs = 2.0 IP)

# Pitchers have to have thrown enough to be judged on rate stats.
# Expressed per team game, like the official NCAA ERA qualifier
# (1.0 IP per team game). Half of that keeps late-inning relievers
# eligible without letting a four-inning cameo lead the staff.
PITCHER_QUAL_IP_PER_GAME <- 0.50
PITCHER_QUAL_IP_FLOOR    <- 10

# Rule-of-thumb flag thresholds. These are scouting
# conventions, NOT league percentiles - the report labels
# them that way. Tune them here in one place.
THRESHOLDS <- list(
  hr_per_game        = 1.10,
  free_bases_per_game = 4.50,
  sb_per_game        = 1.00,
  sac_per_game       = 0.45,
  k_per_game         = 9.00,
  staff_k9_good      = 9.00,
  staff_k9_soft      = 7.50,
  staff_bb9_good     = 3.00,
  staff_bb9_loose    = 4.00,
  staff_whip_good    = 1.20,
  staff_whip_loose   = 1.45,
  percentile_high    = 80,
  percentile_elite   = 90,
  form_swing         = 0.15
)


# ============================================================
# 2. PACKAGES
# ============================================================

required_packages <- c(
  "baseballr", "dplyr", "tidyr", "purrr", "stringr", "tibble",
  "janitor", "lubridate", "scales", "knitr", "rmarkdown",
  "htmltools", "base64enc", "jsonlite"
)

missing_packages <- setdiff(required_packages, rownames(installed.packages()))
if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  install.packages(missing_packages, dependencies = TRUE)
}

invisible(lapply(required_packages, function(pkg) {
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(pkg, character.only = TRUE))
}))

options(timeout = NET_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, scipen = 999)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center", dpi = 120
)

if (utils::packageVersion("baseballr") < "2.0.0") {
  stop(
    "This report requires baseballr 2.0.0 or newer. ",
    "Run install.packages('baseballr') and try again.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

# This report writes styled HTML directly - a hero band, tab bar,
# card grids and inline CSS. Routed through LaTeX none of that
# survives, and pandoc dies on the raw HTML long before you get a
# page. RStudio's "Knit to PDF" button does exactly that, so catch
# it here and say what to do instead of surfacing a LaTeX error.
.output_format <- knitr::opts_knit$get("rmarkdown.pandoc.to")
if (!is.null(.output_format) &&
    !.output_format %in% c("html", "html4", "html5")) {
  stop(
    "This report builds a self-contained HTML page and cannot be knit to ",
    .output_format, ".\n\n",
    "Use the Knit button's default (Knit to HTML), or press Ctrl+Shift+K.\n\n",
    "For a PDF: knit to HTML, open the .html file in Chrome or Edge, press ",
    "Ctrl+P and choose 'Save as PDF'. Turn ON 'Background graphics' in the ",
    "print dialog or the team colours will print white. Every tab is expanded ",
    "automatically when printing, so the PDF contains the whole report.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

CACHE_DIR <- "cache"
dir.create(CACHE_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

```{r helpers}
# ============================================================
# 3. SMALL HELPERS
# ============================================================

`%||%` <- function(x, y) {
  if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0 || all(is.na(x))) y else x
}

as_num <- function(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(x)))

safe_first <- function(x, default = NA_character_) {
  if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0) return(default)
  x <- as.character(x)
  x <- x[!is.na(x) & nzchar(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) default else x[[1]]
}

last_non_na <- function(x, default = NA_real_) {
  idx <- which(!is.na(x))
  if (length(idx) == 0) default else x[[idx[length(idx)]]]
}

n_rows <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x)) return(0L)
  if (is.data.frame(x)) return(nrow(x))
  length(x)
}

slugify <- function(x) {
  x |>
    stringr::str_to_lower() |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("[^a-z0-9]+", "_") |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("^_|_$", "")
}

normalize_team_name <- function(x) {
  x |>
    as.character() |>
    stringr::str_to_lower() |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("[^a-z0-9]", "")
}

# Display name for tables. ESPN sends the same player under more
# than one spelling across games - "Ethan Hawk" in one box score
# and "Ethan P Hawk" in the next - which reads as two players.
# Interior single-letter initials are dropped, but only when the
# first name is a real name: "J.T. Realmuto" and "A.J. Vukovich"
# are left alone, because there the initials ARE the name.
tidy_display_name <- function(x) {
  x <- stringr::str_squish(as.character(x))
  vapply(x, function(one) {
    if (is.na(one) || !nzchar(one)) return(NA_character_)
    tok <- strsplit(one, "\\s+")[[1]]
    if (length(tok) < 3) return(paste(tok, collapse = " "))
    bare <- gsub("[.]", "", tok)
    if (nchar(bare[[1]]) <= 1) return(paste(tok, collapse = " "))
    keep <- rep(TRUE, length(tok))
    interior <- setdiff(seq_along(tok), c(1L, length(tok)))
    keep[interior] <- nchar(bare[interior]) > 1
    paste(tok[keep], collapse = " ")
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}

# Order-insensitive player key. Handles "Smith, John" vs
# "John Smith", accents, punctuation, middle initials and
# generational suffixes, so ESPN and NCAA names can be joined.
norm_person_key <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  x <- iconv(x, from = "UTF-8", to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT", sub = "")
  x <- stringr::str_to_lower(x)
  x <- stringr::str_replace_all(x, "[^a-z ]", " ")
  x <- stringr::str_squish(x)
  vapply(stringr::str_split(x, " "), function(tok) {
    tok <- tok[nchar(tok) > 1]
    tok <- tok[!tok %in% c("jr", "sr", "ii", "iii", "iv")]
    if (length(tok) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(sort(tok), collapse = "_")
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}

# Innings pitched are base-3, not base-10. Doing the math in
# outs is the only way to avoid producing "4.3 IP".
ip_to_outs <- function(x) {
  n     <- as_num(x)
  whole <- floor(n)
  frac  <- round((n - whole) * 10)
  frac[is.na(frac) | !frac %in% c(0, 1, 2)] <- 0
  out <- whole * 3 + frac
  out[is.na(n)] <- NA_real_
  out
}

outs_to_ip_chr <- function(outs) {
  ifelse(is.na(outs), NA_character_, paste0(outs %/% 3, ".", outs %% 3))
}

outs_to_ip_num <- function(outs) outs / 3

# Percentile rank inside a group, NA-safe. Used to put a season
# stat and a recent stat on the same 0-1 scale so they can be
# blended without inventing a composite metric.
rank_pct <- function(x) {
  out <- rep(NA_real_, length(x))
  ok  <- is.finite(x)
  n   <- sum(ok)
  if (n == 0) return(out)
  if (n == 1) {
    out[ok] <- 1
    return(out)
  }
  out[ok] <- (rank(x[ok], ties.method = "average") - 1) / (n - 1)
  out
}

rate_per <- function(numerator, denominator, per = 1) {
  ifelse(
    is.na(denominator) | denominator <= 0,
    NA_real_,
    numerator / denominator * per
  )
}

fmt <- function(x, digits = 2, blank = "—") {
  ifelse(is.na(x) | !is.finite(x), blank, sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x))
}

fmt_avg <- function(x, blank = "—") {
  ifelse(
    is.na(x) | !is.finite(x),
    blank,
    sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", x))
  )
}

fmt_pct <- function(x, digits = 0, blank = "—") {
  ifelse(
    is.na(x) | !is.finite(x),
    blank,
    paste0(sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), 100 * x), "%")
  )
}

fmt_int <- function(x, blank = "—") {
  ifelse(is.na(x) | !is.finite(x), blank, format(round(as_num(x)), trim = TRUE))
}

fmt_chr <- function(x, blank = "—") {
  x <- as.character(x)
  ifelse(is.na(x) | !nzchar(x) | x == "NA", blank, x)
}

# A column that is entirely empty is noise. Printing a wall of NA
# makes a degraded report look like a broken one.
drop_empty_cols <- function(df, keep = character()) {
  if (is.null(df) || ncol(df) == 0) return(df)
  keep_col <- vapply(names(df), function(nm) {
    if (nm %in% keep) return(TRUE)
    vals <- as.character(df[[nm]])
    any(!is.na(vals) & nzchar(vals) & !vals %in% c("—", "NA"))
  }, logical(1))
  df[, keep_col, drop = FALSE]
}

fmt_signed <- function(x, digits = 2, blank = "—") {
  ifelse(is.na(x) | !is.finite(x), blank, sprintf(paste0("%+.", digits, "f"), x))
}

# knitr captures message() output, so progress written that way never
# reaches the console during a knit. Writing straight to stderr does.
progress <- function(...) {
  cat(paste0(..., collapse = ""), "\n", sep = "", file = stderr())
  utils::flush.console()
}

html_escape <- function(x) as.character(htmltools::htmlEscape(as.character(x)))

# Box-score fields arrive as character after harmonization. ESPN sends
# dates as either "2026-04-10" or a full timestamp, and booleans as
# either "TRUE"/"FALSE" or "1"/"0", so both are parsed tolerantly
# rather than assumed.
as_date_safe <- function(x) {
  suppressWarnings(as.Date(substr(as.character(x), 1, 10)))
}

as_lgl <- function(x) {
  x <- stringr::str_to_lower(stringr::str_trim(as.character(x)))
  dplyr::case_when(
    x %in% c("true", "t", "1", "yes")  ~ TRUE,
    x %in% c("false", "f", "0", "no")  ~ FALSE,
    TRUE ~ NA
  )
}

clean_hex <- function(x, fallback = "17324D") {
  x <- gsub("#", "", safe_first(x, fallback))
  if (!grepl("^[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$", x)) fallback else toupper(x)
}

hex_luminance <- function(hex) {
  rgb  <- grDevices::col2rgb(paste0("#", clean_hex(hex))) / 255
  vals <- ifelse(rgb <= 0.03928, rgb / 12.92, ((rgb + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4)
  0.2126 * vals[1] + 0.7152 * vals[2] + 0.0722 * vals[3]
}

contrast_text <- function(hex) if (hex_luminance(hex) > 0.55) "#101820" else "#FFFFFF"

# Find the first column that exists from a list of candidates.
# ESPN and NCAA both rename columns between seasons; this keeps
# a rename from silently turning a real number into NA.
pick_col <- function(df, candidates) {
  if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  hit <- candidates[candidates %in% names(df)]
  if (length(hit) == 0) NA_character_ else hit[[1]]
}

col_or_na <- function(df, candidates, numeric = TRUE) {
  nm <- pick_col(df, candidates)
  if (is.na(nm)) {
    return(rep(if (numeric) NA_real_ else NA_character_, nrow(df)))
  }
  if (numeric) as_num(df[[nm]]) else as.character(df[[nm]])
}
```

```{r data_log_and_cache}
# ============================================================
# 4. PROVENANCE LOG + CACHE
# ============================================================
# Every pull is recorded: where it came from, whether it was
# fresh or cached, when it was fetched, and whether it failed.
# The Data Quality tab prints this. A report that quietly
# renders on half its data is the thing to design against.

AR_STATE <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
AR_STATE$pulls  <- list()
AR_STATE$checks <- list()

log_pull <- function(source, key, status, fetched_at = Sys.time(),
                     rows = NA_integer_, note = "") {
  AR_STATE$pulls[[length(AR_STATE$pulls) + 1]] <- tibble::tibble(
    Source    = source,
    Item      = key,
    Status    = status,
    Retrieved = as.POSIXct(fetched_at),
    Rows      = as.integer(rows),
    Note      = note
  )
  invisible(NULL)
}

log_check <- function(check, result, detail = "") {
  AR_STATE$checks[[length(AR_STATE$checks) + 1]] <- tibble::tibble(
    Check  = check,
    Result = result,
    Detail = detail
  )
  invisible(NULL)
}

pull_log <- function() {
  if (length(AR_STATE$pulls) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())
  dplyr::bind_rows(AR_STATE$pulls)
}

check_log <- function() {
  if (length(AR_STATE$checks) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())
  dplyr::bind_rows(AR_STATE$checks)
}

# Cache keys are versioned so a schema change here can never
# be served a stale object written by an older build.
CACHE_VERSION <- "v2"

cache_path <- function(...) {
  pieces <- vapply(unlist(list(...)), as.character, character(1))
  file.path(
    CACHE_DIR,
    paste0(CACHE_VERSION, "_", paste(pieces, collapse = "_"), ".rds")
  )
}

# A cached answer that later proves wrong has to be removable, or
# one bad resolution outlives every future render.
cache_peek <- function(key) {
  path <- cache_path(key)
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  wrapped <- tryCatch(readRDS(path), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.list(wrapped) && isTRUE(wrapped$.ar_cache)) wrapped$data else NULL
}

cache_poke <- function(key, value) {
  try(
    saveRDS(list(.ar_cache = TRUE, fetched_at = Sys.time(), data = value),
            cache_path(key)),
    silent = TRUE
  )
  invisible(NULL)
}

cache_forget <- function(key) {
  path <- cache_path(key)
  if (file.exists(path)) try(file.remove(path), silent = TRUE)
  invisible(NULL)
}

with_retry <- function(fn, tries = 3, pause = 1.5) {
  for (attempt in seq_len(tries)) {
    result <- try(fn(), silent = TRUE)
    if (!inherits(result, "try-error")) return(result)
    if (attempt < tries) Sys.sleep(pause * attempt)
  }
  stop(attr(result, "condition")$message %||% "request failed", call. = FALSE)
}

# Retries multiply the timeout. Three attempts against a 600
# second timeout is a possible thirty-minute stall on one call,
# which is exactly how a render hangs. Slow sources get one
# attempt and a short clock.
with_timeout <- function(fn, seconds) {
  if (is.null(seconds)) return(fn())
  old <- getOption("timeout")
  options(timeout = seconds)
  on.exit(options(timeout = old), add = TRUE)
  fn()
}

cache_get <- function(key, pull_fn, refresh = FALSE, fallback = NULL,
                      source = "ESPN", label = NULL, retry = TRUE,
                      tries = 3, timeout_seconds = NULL) {
  label <- label %||% paste(key, collapse = " ")
  path  <- cache_path(key)

  if (!refresh && file.exists(path)) {
    wrapped <- tryCatch(readRDS(path), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.list(wrapped) && isTRUE(wrapped$.ar_cache)) {
      log_pull(source, label, "cached", wrapped$fetched_at, n_rows(wrapped$data))
      return(wrapped$data)
    }
  }

  runner <- if (retry && tries > 1) {
    function() with_retry(pull_fn, tries = tries)
  } else {
    pull_fn
  }
  result <- tryCatch(with_timeout(runner, timeout_seconds), error = function(e) {
    log_pull(source, label, "FAILED", Sys.time(), NA_integer_, conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  })

  # Failures are never written to cache, so a bad network day
  # does not become a permanently poisoned cache file.
  if (is.null(result)) return(fallback)

  try(
    saveRDS(
      list(.ar_cache = TRUE, fetched_at = Sys.time(), data = result),
      path
    ),
    silent = TRUE
  )
  log_pull(source, label, "fresh", Sys.time(), n_rows(result))
  result
}

# Binding many ESPN games together fails when a column is
# character in one game and all-NA logical in another. Coercing
# to character first makes the bind deterministic; the columns
# we actually use are typed explicitly downstream.
harmonize_chr <- function(df) {
  if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())
  df <- as.data.frame(df, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  df[] <- lapply(df, function(col) {
    if (is.list(col)) {
      vapply(col, function(z) paste(unlist(z), collapse = "|"), character(1))
    } else {
      as.character(col)
    }
  })
  tibble::as_tibble(df)
}

bind_game_component <- function(bundles, component) {
  parts <- lapply(names(bundles), function(game_id) {
    bundle <- bundles[[game_id]]
    if (is.null(bundle) || !is.list(bundle) || is.null(names(bundle))) {
      return(NULL)
    }
    idx <- which(tolower(names(bundle)) == tolower(component))
    if (length(idx) == 0) return(NULL)
    x <- bundle[[idx[[1]]]]
    if (is.null(x) || nrow(x) == 0) return(NULL)
    x <- harmonize_chr(x)
    if (!"game_id" %in% names(x)) x$game_id <- game_id
    x
  })
  parts <- parts[!vapply(parts, is.null, logical(1))]
  if (length(parts) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())
  dplyr::bind_rows(parts)
}
```

```{r team_lookup}
# ============================================================
# 5. TEAM LOOKUP + LOGO
# ============================================================

resolve_team <- function(query, teams) {
  teams <- janitor::clean_names(teams)
  q     <- normalize_team_name(query)

  name_cols <- intersect(
    c("abbreviation", "display_name", "team", "short_name", "location", "name"),
    names(teams)
  )
  if (length(name_cols) == 0) {
    stop("Could not identify team-name columns in the ESPN team table.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  exact <- rep(FALSE, nrow(teams))
  for (nm in name_cols) {
    exact <- exact | normalize_team_name(teams[[nm]]) == q
  }
  if (any(exact)) return(teams[which(exact)[1], , drop = FALSE])

  blob <- apply(teams[, name_cols, drop = FALSE], 1, function(z) {
    normalize_team_name(paste(z, collapse = " "))
  })
  hits <- which(stringr::str_detect(blob, stringr::fixed(q)))

  if (length(hits) == 0) {
    stop(
      "Could not find a college baseball team matching '", query,
      "'. Try a school name or abbreviation such as UCLA, USC, Oregon.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
  if (length(hits) > 1) {
    log_check(
      "Team name match",
      "AMBIGUOUS",
      paste0(
        "'", query, "' matched ", length(hits), " teams; used ",
        safe_first(teams$display_name[hits[1]], "the first match"), "."
      )
    )
  }
  teams[hits[1], , drop = FALSE]
}

cache_logo <- function(url, team_slug, refresh = FALSE) {
  if (is.na(url) || !nzchar(url)) return(NA_character_)
  path <- file.path(CACHE_DIR, paste0(team_slug, "_logo.png"))
  if (!refresh && file.exists(path)) return(path)

  ok <- tryCatch({
    utils::download.file(url, path, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE, method = "libcurl")
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) FALSE, warning = function(w) FALSE)

  if (!ok || !file.exists(path)) NA_character_ else path
}

file_to_data_uri <- function(path) {
  if (is.na(path) || !file.exists(path)) return(NA_character_)
  paste0("data:image/png;base64,", base64enc::base64encode(path))
}
```

```{r espn_schedule}
# ============================================================
# 6. ESPN SCHEDULE
# ============================================================

pull_team_schedule <- function(team_id, season, refresh = FALSE) {

  parse_score <- function(x) {
    if (is.null(x)) return(NA_real_)
    if (is.atomic(x)) return(as_num(x[[1]]))
    if (is.list(x)) {
      for (nm in c("value", "displayValue", "display_value")) {
        if (!is.null(x[[nm]])) {
          value <- as_num(x[[nm]][[1]])
          if (!is.na(value)) return(value)
        }
      }
    }
    NA_real_
  }

  scalar_chr <- function(x, default = NA_character_) {
    if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0) return(default)
    value <- tryCatch(as.character(x[[1]]), error = function(e) default)
    if (length(value) == 0 || is.na(value) || !nzchar(value)) default else value
  }

  scalar_lgl <- function(x, default = NA) {
    if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0) return(default)
    value <- tryCatch(as.logical(x[[1]]), error = function(e) default)
    if (length(value) == 0) default else value
  }

  fetch_schedule_type <- function(season_type) {
    cache_get(
      c("espn_schedule", team_id, season, season_type),
      function() {
        url <- paste0(
          "https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/baseball/",
          "college-baseball/teams/", team_id,
          "/schedule?season=", season, "&seasontype=", season_type
        )
        raw    <- jsonlite::fromJSON(url, simplifyVector = FALSE)
        events <- raw$events %||% list()
        if (length(events) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

        purrr::map_dfr(events, function(ev) {
          competition <- tryCatch(ev$competitions[[1]], error = function(e) NULL)
          if (is.null(competition)) return(tibble::tibble())

          competitors <- competition$competitors %||% list()
          if (length(competitors) < 2) return(tibble::tibble())

          ids <- vapply(competitors, function(comp) {
            scalar_chr(comp$id %||% comp$team$id %||% NA_character_)
          }, character(1))

          focal_index <- which(ids == as.character(team_id))
          if (length(focal_index) == 0) {
            team_ids <- vapply(competitors, function(comp) {
              scalar_chr(comp$team$id %||% NA_character_)
            }, character(1))
            focal_index <- which(team_ids == as.character(team_id))
          }
          if (length(focal_index) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

          focal_index    <- focal_index[[1]]
          opponent_index <- setdiff(seq_along(competitors), focal_index)[[1]]
          focal          <- competitors[[focal_index]]
          opponent       <- competitors[[opponent_index]]

          team_score_num     <- parse_score(focal$score)
          opponent_score_num <- parse_score(opponent$score)

          status_completed <- scalar_lgl(
            competition$status$type$completed %||% ev$status$type$completed %||% NA
          )
          status_description <- scalar_chr(
            competition$status$type$description %||%
              ev$status$type$description %||% NA_character_
          )
          winner_from_feed <- scalar_lgl(focal$winner %||% NA)

          winner_clean <- dplyr::case_when(
            !is.na(team_score_num) & !is.na(opponent_score_num) &
              team_score_num > opponent_score_num ~ TRUE,
            !is.na(team_score_num) & !is.na(opponent_score_num) &
              team_score_num < opponent_score_num ~ FALSE,
            !is.na(winner_from_feed) ~ winner_from_feed,
            TRUE ~ NA
          )

          completed <- dplyr::case_when(
            !is.na(team_score_num) & !is.na(opponent_score_num) ~ TRUE,
            isTRUE(status_completed) ~ TRUE,
            stringr::str_detect(
              stringr::str_to_lower(status_description %||% ""),
              "final|completed"
            ) ~ TRUE,
            TRUE ~ FALSE
          )

          opponent_name <- scalar_chr(
            opponent$team$displayName %||% opponent$team$shortDisplayName %||%
              opponent$team$name %||% NA_character_
          )
          opponent_abbrev <- scalar_chr(opponent$team$abbreviation %||% NA_character_)
          game_date_raw   <- scalar_chr(ev$date %||% NA_character_)

          tibble::tibble(
            event_id      = scalar_chr(ev$id %||% NA_character_),
            season        = suppressWarnings(as.integer(
              scalar_chr(ev$season$year %||% season)
            )),
            season_type   = season_type,
            game_datetime = suppressWarnings(
              as.POSIXct(game_date_raw, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ", tz = "UTC")
            ),
            game_date     = suppressWarnings(as.Date(substr(game_date_raw, 1, 10))),
            name          = scalar_chr(ev$name %||% NA_character_),
            opponent_id   = scalar_chr(
              opponent$id %||% opponent$team$id %||% NA_character_
            ),
            opponent_name   = opponent_name,
            opponent_abbrev = opponent_abbrev,
            opponent_label  = dplyr::coalesce(opponent_abbrev, opponent_name),
            home_away       = scalar_chr(focal$homeAway %||% NA_character_),
            neutral_site    = scalar_lgl(competition$neutralSite %||% FALSE, FALSE),
            conference_competition = scalar_lgl(
              competition$conferenceCompetition %||% FALSE, FALSE
            ),
            venue_name  = scalar_chr(competition$venue$fullName %||% NA_character_),
            result      = status_description,
            team_score_num     = team_score_num,
            opponent_score_num = opponent_score_num,
            winner_clean = winner_clean,
            completed    = completed
          )
        })
      },
      refresh = refresh,
      fallback = tibble::tibble(),
      source  = "ESPN",
      label   = paste0("schedule (season type ", season_type, ")")
    )
  }

  dplyr::bind_rows(fetch_schedule_type(2), fetch_schedule_type(3)) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(event_id), nzchar(event_id)) |>
    dplyr::distinct(event_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::arrange(game_date, game_datetime)
}

# ============================================================
# CONFERENCE MEMBERSHIP
# ============================================================
# ESPN's schedule feed has no conferenceCompetition field at all
# for college baseball - it is absent, not false - so the old flag
# could never mark a conference game. Instead the team's own
# conference group is looked up, its member team ids are read from
# the conference standings, and a game counts as a conference game
# when the opponent id is in that set. Comparing ids avoids trying
# to match "Saint Mary's Gaels" to "Saint Mary's (CA)" by name.

espn_core_url <- function(...) {
  paste0(
    "https://sports.core.api.espn.com/v2/sports/baseball/leagues/",
    "college-baseball/", paste0(..., collapse = "")
  )
}

# Pure: pull the numeric team ids out of a list of $ref URLs.
ids_from_team_refs <- function(items) {
  if (is.null(items) || length(items) == 0) return(character())
  out <- vapply(items, function(it) {
    ref <- tryCatch(
      it$team$`$ref` %||% it$`$ref` %||% NA_character_,
      error = function(e) NA_character_
    )
    ref <- safe_first(ref, NA_character_)
    if (is.na(ref)) return(NA_character_)
    m <- stringr::str_match(ref, "/teams/([0-9]+)")[, 2]
    if (is.na(m)) NA_character_ else m
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  unique(out[!is.na(out)])
}

espn_conference <- function(team_id, season, refresh = FALSE) {
  blank <- list(id = NA_character_, name = NA_character_, members = character())

  info <- cache_get(
    c("espn_conference", team_id, season),
    function() {
      team_raw <- jsonlite::fromJSON(
        paste0(
          "https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/baseball/",
          "college-baseball/teams/", team_id
        ),
        simplifyVector = FALSE
      )
      grp <- team_raw$team$groups %||% list()
      gid <- safe_first(grp$id %||% NA_character_, NA_character_)
      if (!isTRUE(as.logical(grp$isConference %||% FALSE)) &&
          !is.null(grp$parent$id)) {
        gid <- safe_first(grp$parent$id, gid)
      }
      if (is.na(gid)) stop("no conference group on the team record", call. = FALSE)

      grp_raw <- jsonlite::fromJSON(
        espn_core_url("seasons/", season, "/types/2/groups/", gid),
        simplifyVector = FALSE
      )
      standings_raw <- jsonlite::fromJSON(
        espn_core_url("seasons/", season, "/types/2/groups/", gid, "/standings/0"),
        simplifyVector = FALSE
      )
      entries <- standings_raw$standings %||% standings_raw$entries %||% list()

      list(
        id      = as.character(gid),
        name    = safe_first(
          grp_raw$shortName %||% grp_raw$name %||% NA_character_, NA_character_
        ),
        members = ids_from_team_refs(entries)
      )
    },
    refresh = refresh,
    fallback = NULL,
    source  = "ESPN",
    label   = "conference membership"
  )

  if (is.null(info)) blank else info
}

# Pure: mark conference games from a membership set, falling back to
# whatever the feed's own flag said when membership is unavailable.
mark_conference_games <- function(sched, member_ids, focal_id) {
  members <- setdiff(as.character(member_ids), as.character(focal_id))
  if (length(members) == 0) {
    return(dplyr::mutate(
      sched,
      conference_game = tidyr::replace_na(conference_competition %in% TRUE, FALSE),
      conference_source = "ESPN flag"
    ))
  }
  dplyr::mutate(
    sched,
    conference_game = as.character(opponent_id) %in% members,
    conference_source = "conference membership"
  )
}

get_game_bundle <- function(game_id, refresh = FALSE) {
  cache_get(
    c("espn_game", game_id),
    function() baseballr::espn_college_baseball_game_all(game_id),
    refresh = refresh,
    fallback = NULL,
    source  = "ESPN",
    label   = paste0("game ", game_id)
  )
}

# A series is a run of games against the same opponent on
# consecutive-ish dates. College staffs line up their rotation
# by series slot (Friday / Saturday / Sunday), not by rest days,
# so this is what the starter projection is built on.
add_series_slot <- function(sched, max_gap_days = 1) {
  if (is.null(sched) || nrow(sched) == 0) return(sched)
  sched |>
    dplyr::arrange(game_date, game_datetime) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      .gap = as.numeric(game_date - dplyr::lag(game_date)),
      .new_series = dplyr::coalesce(
        opponent_id != dplyr::lag(opponent_id) | .gap > max_gap_days,
        TRUE
      ),
      series_id   = cumsum(.new_series)
    ) |>
    dplyr::group_by(series_id) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      series_len  = dplyr::n(),
      series_slot = dplyr::row_number(),
      slot_label  = dplyr::if_else(
        series_len >= 3,
        paste0("G", series_slot),
        dplyr::if_else(series_len == 2, paste0("G", series_slot, " (2-gm)"), "Single")
      )
    ) |>
    dplyr::ungroup() |>
    dplyr::select(-.gap, -.new_series)
}
```

```{r ncaa_layer}
# ============================================================
# 7. OFFICIAL NCAA SEASON STATS (SECOND SOURCE)
# ============================================================
# ESPN box scores are excellent for game-level detail but they
# do not publish doubles, triples, HBP or SF per game, which
# means a season slash line cannot honestly be rebuilt from
# them. stats.ncaa.org does publish those. So:
#
#   season rate stats  -> NCAA (official)
#   recent-window work -> ESPN box scores
#   spray / situational-> ESPN play-by-play
#
# and the two sources are reconciled rather than blended.

# stats.ncaa.org requests get one attempt on a short clock. The
# httr timeout is passed through baseballr's ... where it is
# accepted, and quietly skipped where it is not.
ncaa_try <- function(fn, ...) {
  if (requireNamespace("httr", quietly = TRUE)) {
    attempt <- try(fn(..., httr::timeout(NCAA_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)), silent = TRUE)
    if (!inherits(attempt, "try-error")) return(attempt)
    # Any failure here falls through to the plain call. Passing the
    # timeout is a nicety; losing the official season stats because
    # baseballr would not accept it is not a trade worth making.
    progress("  NCAA: retrying without an explicit timeout...")
  }
  fn(...)
}

# Shared by the bundled lookup and the scraped index. Prefers the
# requested season, falls back to the most recent season present -
# a school's id is stable, and an id from last year is a far better
# starting point than no id at all.
match_ncaa_rows <- function(tbl, team_query, team_name, abbreviation,
                            season, division) {
  if (is.null(tbl) || nrow(tbl) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())
  name_col <- pick_col(tbl, c("team_name", "school", "team"))
  if (is.na(name_col)) return(tibble::tibble())

  tbl$.norm <- normalize_team_name(tbl[[name_col]])
  candidates <- unique(normalize_team_name(c(team_name, team_query, abbreviation)))
  candidates <- candidates[nchar(candidates) > 1]

  hits <- tbl[tbl$.norm %in% candidates, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(hits) == 0) {
    for (cand in candidates) {
      if (nchar(cand) < 3) next
      loose <- tbl[
        stringr::str_detect(tbl$.norm, stringr::fixed(cand)) |
          stringr::str_detect(cand, stringr::fixed(tbl$.norm)),
        ,
        drop = FALSE
      ]
      if (nrow(loose) > 0) {
        hits <- loose
        break
      }
    }
  }
  if (nrow(hits) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

  if ("division" %in% names(hits)) {
    div <- as_num(hits$division)
    if (any(div == division, na.rm = TRUE)) {
      hits <- hits[which(div == division), , drop = FALSE]
    }
  }
  if ("year" %in% names(hits)) {
    yr <- as_num(hits$year)
    if (any(yr == season, na.rm = TRUE)) {
      hits <- hits[which(yr == season), , drop = FALSE]
    } else if (any(!is.na(yr))) {
      hits <- hits[which(yr == max(yr, na.rm = TRUE)), , drop = FALSE]
    }
  }
  hits[1, , drop = FALSE]
}

# Gather every team id worth trying, cheapest source first. None of
# these touch the network except the last, which is opt-in. The stats
# endpoint is the only real test of an id, so this returns candidates
# rather than pretending to know which one is right.
# Gather every team id worth trying, cheapest source first. None of
# these touch the network except the last, which is opt-in. The stats
# endpoint is the only real test of an id, so this returns candidates
# rather than pretending to know which one is right.
#
# The lookups are passed in rather than called directly so this can be
# exercised against stand-in tables without a live baseballr install.
ncaa_default_lookups <- function(team_query, team_name) {
  list(
    "bundled school lookup (by name)" =
      function() baseballr::ncaa_school_id_lu(team_name),
    "bundled school lookup (by query)" =
      function() baseballr::ncaa_school_id_lu(team_query),
    "bundled school lookup (full table)" =
      function() baseballr::ncaa_school_id_lu(),
    "packaged teams release" =
      function() baseballr::load_ncaa_baseball_teams()
  )
}

ncaa_candidate_ids <- function(team_query, team_name, abbreviation,
                               season, division = 1,
                               allow_scrape = FALSE, refresh = FALSE,
                               lookups = NULL, scrape_fn = NULL) {
  ids <- character()
  srcs <- character()
  matched_name <- NA_character_

  consider <- function(tbl, label) {
    if (is.null(tbl) || !is.data.frame(tbl) || nrow(tbl) == 0) return(invisible())
    hit <- match_ncaa_rows(janitor::clean_names(tbl), team_query, team_name,
                           abbreviation, season, division)
    if (nrow(hit) == 0) return(invisible())
    found <- as.character(stats::na.omit(c(
      if ("team_id" %in% names(hit)) hit$team_id[[1]],
      if ("season_team_id" %in% names(hit)) hit$season_team_id[[1]]
    )))
    found <- found[nzchar(found)]
    if (length(found) == 0) return(invisible())
    new_ids <- setdiff(found, ids)
    if (length(new_ids) > 0) {
      ids  <<- c(ids, new_ids)
      srcs <<- c(srcs, rep(label, length(new_ids)))
      if (is.na(matched_name) && "team_name" %in% names(hit)) {
        matched_name <<- as.character(hit$team_name[[1]])
      }
    }
    invisible()
  }

  if (is.null(lookups)) lookups <- ncaa_default_lookups(team_query, team_name)
  for (nm in names(lookups)) {
    consider(tryCatch(lookups[[nm]](), error = function(e) NULL), nm)
  }

  # The live index scrape: minutes long, and only when asked for.
  if (length(ids) == 0 && isTRUE(allow_scrape)) {
    if (is.null(scrape_fn)) {
      scrape_fn <- function() {
        cache_get(
          c("ncaa_team_index_v2", season, division),
          function() {
            progress("  NCAA: scraping the D", division,
                     " index - this is the slow path...")
            ncaa_try(baseballr::ncaa_teams, year = season, division = division)
          },
          refresh = refresh,
          fallback = tibble::tibble(),
          source  = "NCAA",
          label   = paste0("D", division, " team index"),
          retry   = FALSE,
          timeout_seconds = NCAA_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
        )
      }
    }
    consider(tryCatch(scrape_fn(), error = function(e) NULL), "scraped index")
  }

  list(
    ids     = ids,
    sources = srcs,
    name    = if (is.na(matched_name)) team_name else matched_name
  )
}

pull_ncaa_stats <- function(ncaa_team_id, season, type, refresh = FALSE) {
  out <- cache_get(
    c("ncaa_stats", ncaa_team_id, season, type),
    function() {
      ncaa_try(
        baseballr::ncaa_team_player_stats,
        team_id = ncaa_team_id, year = season, type = type
      )
    },
    refresh = refresh,
    fallback = tibble::tibble(),
    source  = "NCAA",
    label   = paste0("season ", type),
    retry   = FALSE,
    timeout_seconds = NCAA_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
  )
  if (is.null(out) || nrow(out) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())
  janitor::clean_names(out)
}

build_ncaa_batting <- function(raw) {
  if (is.null(raw) || nrow(raw) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

  name_col <- pick_col(raw, c("player_name", "name", "player"))
  if (is.na(name_col)) return(tibble::tibble())

  out <- tibble::tibble(
    ncaa_name = as.character(raw[[name_col]]),
    key       = norm_person_key(raw[[name_col]]),
    Yr        = col_or_na(raw, c("yr", "class"), numeric = FALSE),
    NPos      = col_or_na(raw, c("pos", "position"), numeric = FALSE),
    G         = col_or_na(raw, c("gp", "g", "games")),
    GS        = col_or_na(raw, c("gs", "games_started")),
    AB        = col_or_na(raw, c("ab")),
    H         = col_or_na(raw, c("h")),
    x2B       = col_or_na(raw, c("x2b", "doubles")),
    x3B       = col_or_na(raw, c("x3b", "triples")),
    HR        = col_or_na(raw, c("hr")),
    TB        = col_or_na(raw, c("tb")),
    RBI       = col_or_na(raw, c("rbi")),
    BB        = col_or_na(raw, c("bb")),
    HBP       = col_or_na(raw, c("hbp")),
    SF        = col_or_na(raw, c("sf")),
    SH        = col_or_na(raw, c("sh")),
    K         = col_or_na(raw, c("k", "so")),
    SB        = col_or_na(raw, c("sb")),
    CS        = col_or_na(raw, c("cs")),
    RBI2out   = col_or_na(raw, c("rbi2out", "rbi_2out"))
  ) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(key))

  # Recompute the slash line from the counting stats rather than
  # trusting the published rate columns. If the recomputation
  # disagrees with the published value, that is itself a finding.
  out |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      PA  = AB + dplyr::coalesce(BB, 0) + dplyr::coalesce(HBP, 0) +
        dplyr::coalesce(SF, 0) + dplyr::coalesce(SH, 0),
      TB  = dplyr::if_else(
        is.na(TB),
        dplyr::coalesce(H, 0) + dplyr::coalesce(x2B, 0) +
          2 * dplyr::coalesce(x3B, 0) + 3 * dplyr::coalesce(HR, 0),
        TB
      ),
      AVG = rate_per(H, AB),
      OBP = rate_per(
        dplyr::coalesce(H, 0) + dplyr::coalesce(BB, 0) + dplyr::coalesce(HBP, 0),
        AB + dplyr::coalesce(BB, 0) + dplyr::coalesce(HBP, 0) + dplyr::coalesce(SF, 0)
      ),
      SLG   = rate_per(TB, AB),
      OPS   = OBP + SLG,
      ISO   = SLG - AVG,
      BBpct = rate_per(BB, PA),
      Kpct  = rate_per(K, PA),
      SBatt = dplyr::coalesce(SB, 0) + dplyr::coalesce(CS, 0),
      SBpct = rate_per(SB, SBatt)
    )
}

build_ncaa_pitching <- function(raw) {
  if (is.null(raw) || nrow(raw) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

  name_col <- pick_col(raw, c("player_name", "name", "player"))
  if (is.na(name_col)) return(tibble::tibble())

  out <- tibble::tibble(
    ncaa_name = as.character(raw[[name_col]]),
    key       = norm_person_key(raw[[name_col]]),
    App       = col_or_na(raw, c("app", "g", "gp")),
    GS        = col_or_na(raw, c("gs")),
    IP_raw    = col_or_na(raw, c("ip")),
    H         = col_or_na(raw, c("h")),
    R         = col_or_na(raw, c("r")),
    ER        = col_or_na(raw, c("er")),
    BB        = col_or_na(raw, c("bb")),
    K         = col_or_na(raw, c("so", "k")),
    HR_A      = col_or_na(raw, c("hr_a", "hr")),
    HB        = col_or_na(raw, c("hb", "hbp")),
    WP        = col_or_na(raw, c("wp")),
    SV        = col_or_na(raw, c("sv"))
  ) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(key))

  out |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Outs = ip_to_outs(IP_raw),
      IP   = outs_to_ip_num(Outs),
      ERA  = rate_per(ER, IP, 9),
      K9   = rate_per(K, IP, 9),
      BB9  = rate_per(BB, IP, 9),
      H9   = rate_per(H, IP, 9),
      KBB  = rate_per(K, BB),
      WHIP = rate_per(dplyr::coalesce(BB, 0) + dplyr::coalesce(H, 0), IP)
    )
}
```

```{r window_builders}
# ============================================================
# 8. RECENT-WINDOW BUILDERS (ESPN BOX SCORES)
# ============================================================
# Everything here is explicitly a WINDOW stat computed from the
# games that actually downloaded. Nothing in this section is a
# season-to-date figure, and nothing here is mixed with one.

# One player, one identity. Two things can split a player in two:
# a different spelling of the name, and ESPN issuing more than one
# athlete_id for the same person. Both are resolved here, once, so
# every table downstream inherits a single row per player rather
# than each table having to defend itself.
build_identity_map <- function(player_df) {
  if (is.null(player_df) || nrow(player_df) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())
  x <- janitor::clean_names(player_df)
  if (!all(c("athlete_id", "athlete_display_name", "team_id") %in% names(x))) {
    return(tibble::tibble())
  }

  base <- tibble::tibble(
    athlete_id = as.character(x$athlete_id),
    team_id    = as.character(x$team_id),
    raw_name   = as.character(x$athlete_display_name)
  ) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(athlete_id), nzchar(athlete_id), !is.na(raw_name)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      clean = tidy_display_name(raw_name),
      key   = norm_person_key(raw_name)
    ) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(key))

  if (nrow(base) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

  # The id that appears most often becomes the one true id.
  canon_id <- base |>
    dplyr::count(team_id, key, athlete_id, name = "rows") |>
    dplyr::group_by(team_id, key) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(rows), athlete_id, .by_group = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 1) |>
    dplyr::ungroup() |>
    dplyr::select(team_id, key, canonical_id = athlete_id)

  # The most-used spelling becomes the display name; ties break to
  # the shortest, which is the one without the middle initial.
  canon_name <- base |>
    dplyr::count(team_id, key, clean, name = "rows") |>
    dplyr::group_by(team_id, key) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(rows), nchar(clean), clean, .by_group = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 1) |>
    dplyr::ungroup() |>
    dplyr::select(team_id, key, Player = clean)

  # Variance is counted on the RAW spellings, before tidying, so the
  # Data Quality tab can report what was actually merged.
  variants <- base |>
    dplyr::group_by(team_id, key) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      id_variants   = dplyr::n_distinct(athlete_id),
      name_variants = dplyr::n_distinct(raw_name),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  canon <- canon_id |>
    dplyr::left_join(canon_name, by = c("team_id", "key")) |>
    dplyr::left_join(variants,   by = c("team_id", "key"))

  base |>
    dplyr::count(athlete_id, team_id, key, name = "rows") |>
    dplyr::group_by(athlete_id) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(rows), .by_group = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 1) |>
    dplyr::ungroup() |>
    dplyr::select(athlete_id, team_id, key) |>
    dplyr::left_join(canon, by = c("team_id", "key"))
}

apply_identity <- function(df, identity) {
  if (is.null(identity) || nrow(identity) == 0 ||
      is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0) {
    return(df)
  }
  df |>
    dplyr::left_join(
      dplyr::select(identity, athlete_id, .canon_id = canonical_id,
                    .canon_name = Player),
      by = "athlete_id"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      athlete_id = dplyr::coalesce(.canon_id, athlete_id),
      Player     = dplyr::coalesce(.canon_name, Player)
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(-.canon_id, -.canon_name)
}

espn_batting_rows <- function(player_df, focal_id, identity = NULL) {
  if (is.null(player_df) || nrow(player_df) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())
  x <- janitor::clean_names(player_df)
  required <- c("team_id", "stat_group", "game_id", "athlete_id",
                "athlete_display_name")
  if (!all(required %in% names(x))) return(tibble::tibble())

  x <- x[
    as.character(x$team_id) == as.character(focal_id) &
      stringr::str_to_lower(x$stat_group) == "batting",
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  if (nrow(x) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

  tibble::tibble(
    game_id    = as.character(x$game_id),
    game_date  = as_date_safe(col_or_na(x, "game_date", numeric = FALSE)),
    athlete_id = as.character(x$athlete_id),
    Player     = as.character(x$athlete_display_name),
    Pos        = col_or_na(x, c("athlete_position_abbreviation"), numeric = FALSE),
    starter    = as_lgl(x$starter),
    bat_order  = col_or_na(x, "bat_order"),
    AB   = col_or_na(x, "ab"),
    R    = col_or_na(x, "r"),
    H    = col_or_na(x, "h"),
    x2B  = col_or_na(x, c("x2b", "doubles")),
    x3B  = col_or_na(x, c("x3b", "triples")),
    HR   = col_or_na(x, "hr"),
    RBI  = col_or_na(x, "rbi"),
    BB   = col_or_na(x, "bb"),
    HBP  = col_or_na(x, c("hbp")),
    K    = col_or_na(x, "k"),
    SB   = col_or_na(x, c("sb")),
    std_avg = col_or_na(x, "avg"),
    std_obp = col_or_na(x, "obp"),
    std_slg = col_or_na(x, "slg")
  ) |>
    apply_identity(identity)
}

  if (is.null(player_df) || nrow(player_df) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

build_batting_window <- function(bat_rows, window_label) {
  if (is.null(bat_rows) || nrow(bat_rows) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

  bat_rows |>
    dplyr::group_by(athlete_id, Player) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      Pos  = safe_first(Pos, ""),
      G    = dplyr::n_distinct(game_id),
      AB   = sum(AB, na.rm = TRUE),
      H    = sum(H, na.rm = TRUE),
      HR   = sum(HR, na.rm = TRUE),
      BB   = sum(BB, na.rm = TRUE),
      K    = sum(K, na.rm = TRUE),
      RBI  = sum(RBI, na.rm = TRUE),
      R    = sum(R, na.rm = TRUE),
      LastGame = suppressWarnings(max(game_date, na.rm = TRUE)),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Window   = window_label,
      wAVG     = rate_per(H, AB),
      # Not OBP. ESPN game box scores do not carry HBP or SF, so
      # a true OBP cannot be built from this window. Reach% is
      # (H + BB) / (AB + BB) and is labelled as such everywhere.
      Reach    = rate_per(H + BB, AB + BB),
      BBpct    = rate_per(BB, AB + BB),
      Kpct     = rate_per(K, AB + BB),
      LastGame = as.Date(ifelse(is.finite(LastGame), LastGame, NA))
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(AB))
}

build_pitching_window <- function(pit_rows, window_label) {
  if (is.null(pit_rows) || nrow(pit_rows) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

  pit_rows |>
    dplyr::group_by(athlete_id, Player) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      App  = dplyr::n_distinct(game_id),
      GS   = sum(starter %in% TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
      Outs = sum(Outs, na.rm = TRUE),
      H    = sum(H, na.rm = TRUE),
      ER   = sum(ER, na.rm = TRUE),
      BB   = sum(BB, na.rm = TRUE),
      K    = sum(K, na.rm = TRUE),
      HR   = sum(HR, na.rm = TRUE),
      Pitches  = sum(Pitches, na.rm = TRUE),
      LastApp  = suppressWarnings(max(game_date, na.rm = TRUE)),
      .groups  = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Window = window_label,
      IPnum  = outs_to_ip_num(Outs),
      IP     = outs_to_ip_chr(Outs),
      ERA    = rate_per(ER, IPnum, 9),
      K9     = rate_per(K, IPnum, 9),
      BB9    = rate_per(BB, IPnum, 9),
      H9     = rate_per(H, IPnum, 9),
      WHIP   = rate_per(BB + H, IPnum),
      PperOut = rate_per(Pitches, Outs),
      LastApp = as.Date(ifelse(is.finite(LastApp), LastApp, NA))
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Outs))
}

# ============================================================
# RECENT PERFORMERS - A SHORT, SEPARATE WINDOW
# ============================================================
# Deliberately kept apart from the season lists. Over five games
# these are small samples and they are labelled that way: the
# at-bats and innings behind every rate are printed on the line.

build_recent_hitters <- function(bat_rows, game_ids, min_ab) {
  if (is.null(bat_rows) || nrow(bat_rows) == 0 || length(game_ids) == 0) {
    return(tibble::tibble())
  }
  rows <- dplyr::filter(bat_rows, game_id %in% game_ids)
  if (nrow(rows) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

  rows |>
    dplyr::group_by(athlete_id, Player) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      G   = dplyr::n_distinct(game_id),
      AB  = sum(AB, na.rm = TRUE),
      H   = sum(H, na.rm = TRUE),
      HR  = sum(HR, na.rm = TRUE),
      BB  = sum(BB, na.rm = TRUE),
      K   = sum(K, na.rm = TRUE),
      RBI = sum(RBI, na.rm = TRUE),
      R   = sum(R, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      AVG   = rate_per(H, AB),
      Reach = rate_per(H + BB, AB + BB),
      Qualified = AB >= min_ab
    ) |>
    dplyr::filter(Qualified) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Reach), dplyr::desc(HR), dplyr::desc(H))
}

build_recent_pitchers <- function(pit_rows, game_ids, min_outs) {
  if (is.null(pit_rows) || nrow(pit_rows) == 0 || length(game_ids) == 0) {
    return(tibble::tibble())
  }
  rows <- dplyr::filter(pit_rows, game_id %in% game_ids)
  if (nrow(rows) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

  rows |>
    dplyr::group_by(athlete_id, Player) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      App  = dplyr::n_distinct(game_id),
      GS   = sum(starter %in% TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
      Outs = sum(Outs, na.rm = TRUE),
      H    = sum(H, na.rm = TRUE),
      ER   = sum(ER, na.rm = TRUE),
      BB   = sum(BB, na.rm = TRUE),
      K    = sum(K, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      IPnum = outs_to_ip_num(Outs),
      IP    = outs_to_ip_chr(Outs),
      ERA   = rate_per(ER, IPnum, 9),
      WHIP  = rate_per(BB + H, IPnum),
      K9    = rate_per(K, IPnum, 9),
      Qualified = Outs >= min_outs
    ) |>
    dplyr::filter(Qualified) |>
    dplyr::arrange(ERA, WHIP, dplyr::desc(K9))
}

build_expected_lineup <- function(bat_rows, recent_lineup_games = 5) {
  if (is.null(bat_rows) || nrow(bat_rows) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

  starts <- bat_rows |>
    dplyr::filter(
      starter %in% TRUE,
      !is.na(bat_order), bat_order >= 1, bat_order <= 9
    )
  if (nrow(starts) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

  recent_ids <- starts |>
    dplyr::distinct(game_id, game_date) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(game_date)) |>
    dplyr::slice_head(n = recent_lineup_games)

  starts <- dplyr::semi_join(starts, recent_ids, by = c("game_id", "game_date"))

  players <- starts |>
    dplyr::group_by(athlete_id, Player) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      Starts     = dplyr::n_distinct(game_id),
      MedianSpot = stats::median(bat_order, na.rm = TRUE),
      AvgSpot    = mean(bat_order, na.rm = TRUE),
      Pos        = safe_first(Pos, ""),
      LastStart  = suppressWarnings(max(game_date, na.rm = TRUE)),
      .groups    = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Spot = pmin(9, pmax(1, round(MedianSpot))),
      LastStart = as.Date(ifelse(is.finite(LastStart), LastStart, NA))
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(MedianSpot, dplyr::desc(Starts))

  # One player per projected spot, but keep the runner-up so the
  # staff can see where a lineup is genuinely unsettled.
  primary <- players |>
    dplyr::group_by(Spot) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Starts), AvgSpot, .by_group = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::mutate(rank_in_spot = dplyr::row_number()) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()

  primary |>
    dplyr::group_by(Spot) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      Player    = Player[rank_in_spot == 1][1],
      Pos       = Pos[rank_in_spot == 1][1],
      Starts    = Starts[rank_in_spot == 1][1],
      LastStart = LastStart[rank_in_spot == 1][1],
      Alternate = {
        alt <- Player[rank_in_spot == 2]
        if (length(alt) == 0 || is.na(alt[1])) "—" else
          paste0(alt[1], " (", Starts[rank_in_spot == 2][1], ")")
      },
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(Spot)
}
```

```{r rotation_and_bullpen}
# ============================================================
# 9. ROTATION PROJECTION BY SERIES SLOT
# ============================================================
# The old model scored starters on rest days and printed a
# percentage. College staffs do not line up on rest days, they
# line up on series slot - Friday, Saturday, Sunday, midweek -
# and a percentage implies a precision this data cannot carry.
# This version scores recency-weighted slot history and reports
# a tier plus the evidence behind it.

build_rotation_projection <- function(pit_rows, sched_completed, next_game,
                                      half_life_days = 21) {
  if (is.null(pit_rows) || nrow(pit_rows) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

  starts <- pit_rows |>
    dplyr::filter(starter %in% TRUE) |>
    dplyr::distinct(athlete_id, Player, game_id, game_date)
  if (nrow(starts) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

  slot_lookup <- sched_completed |>
    dplyr::select(game_id = event_id, series_slot, series_len, slot_label)

  starts <- starts |>
    dplyr::left_join(slot_lookup, by = "game_id")

  target_slot <- next_game$series_slot %||% NA_real_
  target_date <- next_game$game_date %||% (max(starts$game_date, na.rm = TRUE) + 5)

  scored <- starts |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      days_ago  = as.numeric(target_date - game_date),
      recency_w = 0.5^(days_ago / half_life_days),
      slot_w    = dplyr::case_when(
        is.na(target_slot) | is.na(series_slot) ~ 0.60,
        series_slot == target_slot ~ 1.00,
        abs(series_slot - target_slot) == 1 ~ 0.35,
        TRUE ~ 0.15
      )
    ) |>
    dplyr::group_by(athlete_id, Player) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      Starts    = dplyr::n(),
      LastStart = max(game_date, na.rm = TRUE),
      SlotMix   = {
        tab <- table(slot_label[!is.na(slot_label)])
        if (length(tab) == 0) "—" else
          paste(paste0(names(tab), "×", as.integer(tab)), collapse = " · ")
      },
      SlotStarts = sum(series_slot == target_slot, na.rm = TRUE),
      RawScore   = sum(recency_w * slot_w, na.rm = TRUE),
      TypicalRest = {
        gaps <- diff(sort(game_date))
        gaps <- as.numeric(gaps)
        gaps <- gaps[gaps >= 3 & gaps <= 14]
        if (length(gaps) == 0) NA_real_ else stats::median(gaps)
      },
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      DaysToGame = as.numeric(target_date - LastStart),
      # A starter who threw two days ago is not starting.
      RestPenalty = dplyr::case_when(
        is.na(DaysToGame) ~ 1,
        DaysToGame < 3    ~ 0.10,
        DaysToGame < 4    ~ 0.60,
        TRUE              ~ 1
      ),
      Score = RawScore * RestPenalty
    )

  total <- sum(scored$Score, na.rm = TRUE)

  scored |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Share = if (is.finite(total) && total > 0) Score / total else NA_real_,
      Projection = dplyr::case_when(
        is.na(Share)     ~ "Unclear",
        Share >= 0.35    ~ "Likely",
        Share >= 0.15    ~ "Possible",
        TRUE             ~ "Unlikely"
      )
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Score)) |>
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 6)
}


# ============================================================
# 10. BULLPEN WORKLOAD
# ============================================================

build_bullpen_usage <- function(pit_rows, as_of_date, window_days = 7) {
  if (is.null(pit_rows) || nrow(pit_rows) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

  relief <- pit_rows |> dplyr::filter(!(starter %in% TRUE))
  if (nrow(relief) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

  recent <- relief |>
    dplyr::filter(game_date >= as_of_date - window_days, game_date <= as_of_date)

  # Back-to-back days is the usage flag a staff actually acts on.
  b2b <- relief |>
    dplyr::distinct(athlete_id, game_date) |>
    dplyr::arrange(athlete_id, game_date) |>
    dplyr::group_by(athlete_id) |>
    dplyr::mutate(gap = as.numeric(game_date - dplyr::lag(game_date))) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      B2B = sum(gap == 1 & game_date >= as_of_date - window_days, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  base <- relief |>
    dplyr::group_by(athlete_id, Player) |>
    dplyr::summarise(Last = max(game_date, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  usage <- recent |>
    dplyr::group_by(athlete_id, Player) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      App7     = dplyr::n_distinct(game_id),
      Outs7    = sum(Outs, na.rm = TRUE),
      Pitches7 = sum(Pitches, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups  = "drop"
    )

  base |>
    dplyr::left_join(usage, by = c("athlete_id", "Player")) |>
    dplyr::left_join(b2b, by = "athlete_id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      App7     = tidyr::replace_na(App7, 0L),
      Outs7    = tidyr::replace_na(Outs7, 0),
      Pitches7 = tidyr::replace_na(Pitches7, 0),
      B2B      = tidyr::replace_na(B2B, 0L),
      DaysRest = as.numeric(as_of_date - Last),
      IP7      = outs_to_ip_chr(Outs7),
      Status   = dplyr::case_when(
        App7 >= 3 | Pitches7 >= 60 | B2B >= 1 ~ "HEAVY",
        App7 >= 2 | Pitches7 >= 35            ~ "WATCH",
        TRUE                                  ~ "FRESH"
      )
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(DaysRest, dplyr::desc(Pitches7)) |>
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 12)
}


# ============================================================
# 11. TEAM BOX-SCORE RATES
# ============================================================
# Returns the rates AND a record of which underlying fields
# actually resolved, so a renamed ESPN column shows up as a
# disclosed gap instead of a silent zero.

build_team_rates <- function(team_df, focal_id) {
  empty <- tibble::tibble(
    Games = 0, HR_G = NA_real_, BB_G = NA_real_, HBP_G = NA_real_,
    K_G = NA_real_, SB_G = NA_real_, SAC_G = NA_real_,
    P_K_G = NA_real_, P_BB_G = NA_real_
  )
  missing_note <- character()

  if (is.null(team_df) || nrow(team_df) == 0) {
    return(list(rates = empty, missing = "team box scores unavailable"))
  }

  x <- janitor::clean_names(team_df)
  if (!"team_id" %in% names(x)) {
    return(list(rates = empty, missing = "team_id column missing"))
  }
  x <- x[as.character(x$team_id) == as.character(focal_id), , drop = FALSE]

  games <- dplyr::n_distinct(x$game_id)
  if (games == 0) return(list(rates = empty, missing = "no team rows for this team"))

  total_for <- function(label, candidates) {
    nm <- pick_col(x, candidates)
    if (is.na(nm)) {
      missing_note <<- c(missing_note, label)
      return(NA_real_)
    }
    sum(as_num(x[[nm]]), na.rm = TRUE)
  }

  rates <- tibble::tibble(
    Games  = games,
    HR_G   = total_for("HR",  c("batting_home_runs", "batting_hr")) / games,
    BB_G   = total_for("BB",  c("batting_walks", "batting_bb")) / games,
    HBP_G  = total_for("HBP", c("batting_hit_by_pitch", "batting_hit_by_pitches",
                                "batting_hbp")) / games,
    K_G    = total_for("K",   c("batting_strikeouts", "batting_k")) / games,
    SB_G   = total_for("SB",  c("batting_stolen_bases", "batting_sb")) / games,
    SAC_G  = total_for("SAC", c("batting_sac_hits", "batting_sacrifice_hits",
                                "batting_sac_bunts")) / games,
    P_K_G  = total_for("K thrown", c("pitching_strikeouts", "pitching_k")) / games,
    P_BB_G = total_for("BB issued", c("pitching_walks", "pitching_bb")) / games
  )

  list(
    rates = rates,
    missing = if (length(missing_note) == 0) "" else
      paste(unique(missing_note), collapse = ", ")
  )
}
```

```{r pbp_engine}
# ============================================================
# 12. PLAY-BY-PLAY ENGINE
# ============================================================
# Written against the real ESPN college feed, which looks like:
#
#   "S. Kretsch pitches to D. West"
#   "Pitch 4 : Strike 3 Swinging"
#   "D. West struck out swinging. "
#   "M. Levu singled to right, R. Cholowsky to third. "
#
# Three consequences drive the design:
#   1. Batters are named by initial and surname, not in full.
#   2. The feed is pitch-level, so pitch rows and pitcher-matchup
#      rows have to be dropped before anything is counted.
#   3. scoreValue is 0 even on scoring plays - runs live in the
#      running awayScore / homeScore, so they are differenced.
#
# Events are attributed only to the player named at the START of
# the play, so "M. Levu singled to right, R. Cholowsky to third"
# credits the single to Levu and not to Cholowsky.

PA_RESULT_REGEX <- paste(
  "singled", "doubled", "tripled", "homered", "home run", "grand slam",
  "walked", "struck out", "strikeout", "grounded", "flied", "lined",
  "popped", "fouled out", "flied into", "hit by pitch", "hit into",
  "reached on", "fielder's choice", "sacrificed", "sacrifice fly",
  "sac fly", "infield fly", "out at first", "grounded into",
  sep = "|"
)

# Rows that are not events: pitch tracking, the pitcher-batter
# matchup header, and inning banners.
NON_EVENT_REGEX <- paste(
  "^pitch\\s*\\d+\\s*:",
  "\\bpitches to\\b",
  "^(top|bottom|middle|end) of the\\b",
  "^(start|end) of\\b",
  "^game (start|end)",
  sep = "|"
)

# Direction is FIELD direction, not pull/oppo: ESPN publishes no
# batting handedness for college players, so pull side is not
# knowable. Gap balls go to the half of the field they were hit
# toward. Bare fielder words are included because this feed writes
# "to right" and "to short", not "to right field" / "to shortstop".
FIELD_MAP <- c(
  "left center" = "Left", "left centerfield" = "Left", "lc" = "Left",
  "left field" = "Left", "left fielder" = "Left", "left side" = "Left",
  "left" = "Left", "lf" = "Left", "shortstop" = "Left", "ss" = "Left",
  "short" = "Left", "third base" = "Left", "third baseman" = "Left",
  "third" = "Left", "3b" = "Left",
  "center field" = "Center", "centerfield" = "Center", "center" = "Center",
  "cf" = "Center", "the middle" = "Center", "middle" = "Center",
  "pitcher" = "Center", "the mound" = "Center", "catcher" = "Center",
  "right center" = "Right", "right centerfield" = "Right", "rc" = "Right",
  "right field" = "Right", "right fielder" = "Right", "right side" = "Right",
  "right" = "Right", "rf" = "Right", "first base" = "Right",
  "first baseman" = "Right", "first" = "Right", "1b" = "Right",
  "second base" = "Right", "second baseman" = "Right", "second" = "Right",
  "2b" = "Right"
)

build_field_regex <- function() {
  keys <- names(FIELD_MAP)
  keys <- keys[order(-nchar(keys))]
  paste0(
    "(?:to|through|down|up|into|over|toward|off)\\s+(?:the\\s+)?(",
    paste(keys, collapse = "|"), ")\\b"
  )
}
FIELD_REGEX <- build_field_regex()

# "R. Cholowsky" and "Roch Cholowsky" both reduce to r_cholowsky,
# which is what lets the play text join to the box-score roster.
initial_last_key <- function(x) {
  x <- iconv(as.character(x), from = "UTF-8", to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT", sub = "")
  x <- stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_replace_all(stringr::str_to_lower(x),
                                                    "[^a-z ]", " "))
  vapply(stringr::str_split(x, " "), function(tok) {
    tok <- tok[nzchar(tok)]
    tok <- tok[!tok %in% c("jr", "sr", "ii", "iii", "iv")]
    if (length(tok) < 2) return(NA_character_)
    paste0(substr(tok[[1]], 1, 1), "_", tok[[length(tok)]])
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}

last_name_key <- function(x) {
  x <- iconv(as.character(x), from = "UTF-8", to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT", sub = "")
  x <- stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_replace_all(stringr::str_to_lower(x),
                                                    "[^a-z ]", " "))
  vapply(stringr::str_split(x, " "), function(tok) {
    tok <- tok[nchar(tok) > 1]
    tok <- tok[!tok %in% c("jr", "sr", "ii", "iii", "iv")]
    if (length(tok) == 0) return(NA_character_)
    tok[[length(tok)]]
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}

# Three lookups, tried in order of how much evidence they carry.
# A bare surname is only allowed to match when it is unique across
# both rosters, so "Hawk" is never guessed at when two Hawks played.
build_name_lookups <- function(roster) {
  if (is.null(roster) || nrow(roster) == 0) {
    return(list(full = character(), initial = character(), last = character()))
  }
  full <- roster$athlete_id
  names(full) <- roster$key

  il_keys <- initial_last_key(roster$Player)
  ok_il   <- !is.na(il_keys) & !duplicated(il_keys) &
    !il_keys %in% il_keys[duplicated(il_keys)]
  initial <- roster$athlete_id[ok_il]
  names(initial) <- il_keys[ok_il]

  ln_keys <- last_name_key(roster$Player)
  ok_ln   <- !is.na(ln_keys) & !ln_keys %in% ln_keys[duplicated(ln_keys)]
  last <- roster$athlete_id[ok_ln]
  names(last) <- ln_keys[ok_ln]

  list(full = full, initial = initial, last = last)
}

match_leading_player <- function(text, lookups) {
  clean <- stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_replace_all(text, "^[^A-Za-z]+", ""))
  best  <- rep(NA_character_, length(clean))

  for (k in c(4, 3, 2, 1)) {
    prefix <- stringr::str_extract(clean, paste0("^(?:\\S+\\s+){", k - 1, "}\\S+"))

    if (k >= 2) {
      hit  <- unname(lookups$full[norm_person_key(prefix)])
      take <- is.na(best) & !is.na(hit)
      best[take] <- hit[take]

      hit  <- unname(lookups$initial[initial_last_key(prefix)])
      take <- is.na(best) & !is.na(hit)
      best[take] <- hit[take]
    }

    hit  <- unname(lookups$last[last_name_key(prefix)])
    take <- is.na(best) & !is.na(hit)
    best[take] <- hit[take]
  }
  best
}

# Runner state, clamped at zero, evaluated BEFORE each event.
state_before <- function(delta) {
  s <- 0
  out <- numeric(length(delta))
  for (i in seq_along(delta)) {
    out[i] <- s
    s <- max(0, s + delta[i])
  }
  out
}

# Runs get their own ledger rather than riding on event rows.
# Two lessons are baked in here. Summing scoreValue double-counts,
# because pitch rows and the result row of the same at-bat both
# carry it. Differencing the score on filtered rows loses any run
# whose delta landed on a row that was dropped. So the ledger is
# built from the running score across EVERY row, before any
# filtering, and attribution comes from which side's score moved -
# no dependence on team_id or the inning-half label.
build_run_ledger <- function(plays_df, focal_id, sched_completed) {
  if (is.null(plays_df) || nrow(plays_df) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())
  x <- janitor::clean_names(plays_df)
  if (!all(c("game_id", "away_score", "home_score") %in% names(x))) {
    return(tibble::tibble())
  }

  rows <- tibble::tibble(
    game_id    = as.character(x$game_id),
    inning     = col_or_na(x, c("period_number")),
    away_score = col_or_na(x, c("away_score")),
    home_score = col_or_na(x, c("home_score"))
  ) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(inning), inning >= 1)

  if (nrow(rows) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())

  # Highest score REACHED in each inning, then difference those.
  # Row order inside an inning is irrelevant, no row needs to be
  # the one "carrying" the run, and dropping rows cannot lose one.
  # Only the innings themselves need to be in order, and they are
  # sorted here explicitly.
  per_inning <- rows |>
    dplyr::group_by(game_id, Inning = inning) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      away_max = suppressWarnings(max(away_score, na.rm = TRUE)),
      home_max = suppressWarnings(max(home_score, na.rm = TRUE)),
      .groups  = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      away_max = dplyr::if_else(is.finite(away_max), away_max, NA_real_),
      home_max = dplyr::if_else(is.finite(home_max), home_max, NA_real_)
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(game_id, Inning) |>
    dplyr::group_by(game_id) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      # cummax guards against a mid-inning correction reading low
      away_cum = cummax(tidyr::replace_na(away_max, 0)),
      home_cum = cummax(tidyr::replace_na(home_max, 0)),
      d_away   = away_cum - dplyr::lag(away_cum, default = 0),
      d_home   = home_cum - dplyr::lag(home_cum, default = 0)
    ) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()

  ctx <- sched_completed |>
    dplyr::select(game_id = event_id, home_away)

  per_inning |>
    dplyr::left_join(ctx, by = "game_id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      focal_is_home = stringr::str_to_lower(dplyr::coalesce(home_away, "")) == "home",
      FocalRuns = dplyr::if_else(focal_is_home, d_home, d_away),
      OppRuns   = dplyr::if_else(focal_is_home, d_away, d_home)
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(game_id, Inning, FocalRuns, OppRuns)
}

parse_pbp <- function(plays_df, focal_id, roster, sched_completed) {
  empty <- tibble::tibble()
  if (is.null(plays_df) || nrow(plays_df) == 0) return(empty)

  x <- janitor::clean_names(plays_df)
  if (!all(c("game_id", "text") %in% names(x))) return(empty)

  raw <- tibble::tibble(
    game_id = as.character(x$game_id),
    seq     = col_or_na(x, c("sequence_number", "id")),
    at_bat  = col_or_na(x, c("at_bat_id"), numeric = FALSE),
    text    = as.character(x$text),
    team_id = col_or_na(x, c("team_id"), numeric = FALSE),
    inning  = col_or_na(x, c("period_number")),
    half    = col_or_na(x, c("period_type", "period_display_value"),
                        numeric = FALSE),
    away_score = col_or_na(x, c("away_score")),
    home_score = col_or_na(x, c("home_score"))
  ) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(text), nzchar(stringr::str_squish(text))) |>
    dplyr::arrange(game_id, seq)

  if (nrow(raw) == 0) return(empty)

  # Runs are NOT taken from these rows - see build_run_ledger.
  ev <- raw |>
    dplyr::mutate(lower = stringr::str_to_lower(stringr::str_squish(text))) |>
    dplyr::filter(!stringr::str_detect(lower, NON_EVENT_REGEX)) |>
    dplyr::distinct(game_id, at_bat, text, .keep_all = TRUE)

  if (nrow(ev) == 0) return(empty)

  ctx <- sched_completed |>
    dplyr::select(game_id = event_id, home_away, opponent_label, d1_opponent,
                  game_date)

  ev <- dplyr::left_join(ev, ctx, by = "game_id")

  lookups <- build_name_lookups(roster)

  ev <- ev |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      half_lower = stringr::str_to_lower(dplyr::coalesce(half, "")),
      bats_home  = dplyr::case_when(
        stringr::str_detect(half_lower, "bottom") ~ TRUE,
        stringr::str_detect(half_lower, "top")    ~ FALSE,
        TRUE ~ NA
      ),
      home_is_focal = stringr::str_to_lower(dplyr::coalesce(home_away, "")) == "home",
      # Which side is batting is derived from the inning half, which
      # is unambiguous. team_id is only the fallback.
      actor_id = match_leading_player(text, lookups),
      is_pa    = stringr::str_detect(lower, PA_RESULT_REGEX),
      is_hit   = stringr::str_detect(lower, "singled|doubled|tripled|homered|home run|grand slam"),
      is_hr    = stringr::str_detect(lower, "homered|home run|grand slam"),
      is_bb    = stringr::str_detect(lower, "\\bwalked\\b|intentionally walked"),
      is_hbp   = stringr::str_detect(lower, "hit by pitch"),
      is_k     = stringr::str_detect(lower, "struck out|strikeout"),
      is_roe   = stringr::str_detect(lower, "reached on (an )?error"),
      is_bunt  = stringr::str_detect(lower, "\\bbunt"),
      is_sac_bunt = stringr::str_detect(lower, "sacrifice bunt|sacrificed"),
      is_steal = stringr::str_detect(lower, "\\bstole\\b|stolen base"),
      is_cs    = stringr::str_detect(lower, "caught stealing"),
      is_po    = stringr::str_detect(lower, "picked off|pickoff"),
      # Runs the play TEXT actually names. A home run scores the
      # batter without the text saying "scored", so he is added.
      # This is deliberately independent of the score columns -
      # it measures whether the text parse is seeing the game.
      text_runs = stringr::str_count(lower, "\\bscored\\b") +
        as.numeric(stringr::str_detect(lower, "homered|home run|grand slam")),
      bb_type = dplyr::case_when(
        stringr::str_detect(lower, "homered|home run|grand slam") ~ "HR",
        stringr::str_detect(lower, "popped|pop up|pop fly|infield fly|fouled out") ~ "PU",
        stringr::str_detect(lower, "\\blined\\b|line drive") ~ "LD",
        stringr::str_detect(lower, "flied|fly ball|sacrifice fly|sac fly") ~ "FB",
        stringr::str_detect(lower, "grounded|ground ball|bunt|infield single") ~ "GB",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),
      direction = unname(FIELD_MAP[stringr::str_match(lower, FIELD_REGEX)[, 2]])
    )

  # Runners in scoring position, derived and deliberately
  # conservative. A runner advance is written as a clause after a
  # comma - "singled to right, R. Cholowsky to third" - which is
  # what separates it from a fielder ("grounded out to third").
  ev <- ev |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      gain = as.numeric(
        stringr::str_detect(lower, "doubled|tripled|stole second|stole third") |
          stringr::str_detect(lower, ",[^,]*\\bto (second|third)\\b") |
          stringr::str_detect(lower, "advanced to (second|third)")
      ),
      loss = stringr::str_count(lower, "scored") +
        as.numeric(stringr::str_detect(
          lower,
          "caught stealing|picked off|doubled off|out at third|out at home|thrown out at"
        )),
      delta = gain - loss
    ) |>
    dplyr::group_by(game_id, inning, half) |>
    dplyr::mutate(risp_before = state_before(delta) > 0) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()

  ev <- ev |>
    dplyr::group_by(game_id, actor_id) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      pa_index = dplyr::if_else(
        is_pa & !is.na(actor_id), cumsum(is_pa & !is.na(actor_id)), NA_integer_
      )
    ) |>
    dplyr::ungroup() |>
    dplyr::group_by(game_id, inning, half) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      inning_pa = dplyr::if_else(is_pa, cumsum(is_pa), NA_integer_),
      leadoff   = inning_pa == 1
    ) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()

  # Whose half-inning it is: the batter's own team settles it when
  # the batter was identified, the inning half when he wasn't, and
  # the play's team_id only as a last resort.
  ev |>
    dplyr::left_join(
      dplyr::select(roster, actor_id = athlete_id, actor = Player,
                    actor_team = team_id),
      by = "actor_id"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      is_focal = dplyr::case_when(
        !is.na(actor_team) ~ actor_team == as.character(focal_id),
        !is.na(bats_home)  ~ bats_home == home_is_focal,
        !is.na(team_id)    ~ team_id == as.character(focal_id),
        TRUE ~ NA
      ),
      is_focal = tidyr::replace_na(is_focal, FALSE)
    )
}

pbp_coverage <- function(events) {
  if (is.null(events) || nrow(events) == 0) {
    return(tibble::tibble(
      Metric = "Play-by-play", Value = "no plays parsed", Detail = ""
    ))
  }
  pa <- dplyr::filter(events, is_pa)
  bip <- dplyr::filter(pa, !is_k, !is_bb, !is_hbp)
  tibble::tibble(
    Metric = c(
      "Event rows kept",
      "Plate appearances identified",
      "PA attributed to a named batter",
      "Balls in play with a resolved direction",
      "Balls in play with a resolved type"
    ),
    Value = c(
      as.character(nrow(events)),
      as.character(nrow(pa)),
      fmt_pct(mean(!is.na(pa$actor_id))),
      fmt_pct(mean(!is.na(bip$direction))),
      fmt_pct(mean(!is.na(bip$bb_type)))
    ),
    Detail = c(
      "pitch-tracking and matchup rows removed",
      "text matched a plate-appearance result",
      "leading-name match against the box-score roster",
      "left / center / right, from the play text",
      "GB / LD / FB / PU / HR"
    )
  )
}
```
